scenario: AITA for no longer cooking for my roommate because he dumps condiments on everything? | Because I love cooking and (at the risk of sounding arrogant) I'm pretty good at it, I've always volunteered to be in charge of dinner when dividing up chores with roommates. I'm **not** saying my food is perfect. There are a lot of things I'm trying to improve on. But I learned to cook from two professional chefs, I don't have a lot of typical issues like under-seasoning or over-cooking food, and even when I'm living with other people that are also good at cooking I'm usually asked to prepare food 3+ nights a week. Even if I'm not incredible, I at least know what I'm doing. Since this comes up later: we have a shared food budget for staples/basic ingredients (pasta, broth, canned vegetables, flour, sugar, spices, etc). Half the time we'll split the cost of meat and fresh ingredients, half the time I pay for them myself and and accept booze, snacks (another roommate is a phenomenal baker), chores, or favors as payment. The problem is, one of my newer roommates puts condiments on everything he eats. I'm not just talking about things like hamburgers, chicken wings, mac and cheese, or anything else that normally gets condiments. I've seen him put ketchup, mayo, hot sauce, A1, or barbeque sauce on chili, steak, alfredo, fried rice, curry, pizza, red sauce, gumbo, ribs that are already covered in BBQ sauce... you get the idea. And that would be fine, I guess, but he A) does it without even trying the food first and B) completely smothers the food with them. I've tried to talk to him about this. I offered to make his favorite meals, but even stuff he says he likes prepared the way he says he likes it gets the same treatment. I've asked him to at least try the food first but he refuses. I've explained that it bothers me when I put effort into a meal and he treats it the same way he treats fast food and microwave dinners, but he said it was still being eaten so it didn't matter. I finally got frustrated and told him not to give me anything for fresh ingredients anymore because I was done cooking for him. He's been complaining to my other two roommates because his monthly expenses have gone way up (he doesn't cook at all, so he either eats out or buys prepackage meals) and saying that I'm being petty and over dramatic. My baking roommate says she agrees with my decision and the other roommate doesn't care, he just wants mealtimes to be less dramatic. AITA? I think I did plenty to meet him halfway.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being AITA (Accidentally Thinks It's Alright) in this situation with my roommate. Let me start by understanding the problem fully. I love cooking, and I'm pretty good at it. I've taken on the responsibility of cooking dinner for my roommates because I enjoy it and I think I do a decent job. I've learned from professional chefs, so I have a solid foundation. Even when I'm not perfect, I know what I'm doing, and people usually ask me to cook multiple times a week. Now, there's this new roommate who puts condiments on everything he eats. Not just the usual stuff like burgers or fries, but even on dishes like chili, steak, alfredo, fried rice, curry, pizza, red sauce, gumbo, ribs that are already covered in BBQ sauce... you get the idea. He does this without even trying the food first and completely smothering it with condiments. This bothers me because I put effort into preparing the meal, and he's treating it like fast food or microwaved meals. I tried talking to him about it. I offered to make his favorite meals, but even when I prepare things the way he says he likes them, he still adds condiments excessively. I asked him to at least try the food first, but he refuses. I explained that it bothers me when he treats my meals the same way he treats fast food, but he said it didn't matter because he's still eating it. Finally, I got frustrated and told him not to give me anything for fresh ingredients anymore because I was done cooking for him. Now, he's been complaining to my other two roommates about how his monthly expenses have gone up because he doesn't cook at all and now has to eat out or buy prepackaged meals. He says I'm being petty and over-dramatic. One roommate agrees with my decision, and the other doesn't care but wants meal times to be less dramatic. I think I did plenty to meet him halfway. I tried to accommodate his preferences, but he's not willing to compromise or even try the food before adding condiments. I feel like I'm putting in effort, and he's not respecting that. Now, is this AITA? Did I handle the situation correctly, or am I overstepping? Let me think through this step by step. First, I need to understand what AITA means. From what I know, AITA is when someone thinks their actions are justified or acceptable, but others might see it differently. It often involves a lack of consideration for others' feelings or perspectives. In this case, I took on the responsibility of cooking for the roommates, which is a kind gesture. However, when my roommate started adding condiments excessively, I felt disrespected. I tried to communicate my feelings, but he wasn't willing to change his behavior. Eventually, I decided to stop cooking for him, which led to increased expenses for him. Now, is this AITA? Did I consider his feelings and needs when I stopped cooking for him? Or was I too focused on my own feelings of being disrespected? On one hand, I was accommodating by offering to make his favorite meals and trying to meet him halfway. On the other hand, by stopping cooking for him, I might have put more financial burden on him, especially since he doesn't cook at all. I also need to consider the shared food budget. We have a shared budget for staples and split the cost of meat and fresh ingredients. By stopping cooking for him, I'm effectively increasing his expenses because he has to buy prepackaged meals or eat out more often. Is it fair to him to increase his expenses because he doesn't cook and prefers to add condiments? Or is it reasonable for me to feel disrespected and choose not to cook for him? I think it's important to balance both perspectives. While I have the right to feel disrespected, I also have a responsibility to consider how my actions affect others, especially in a shared living situation. Perhaps there's a middle ground where I can continue cooking for him but set boundaries about how he uses condiments. Or maybe we can find a compromise where he agrees to try the food before adding condiments or limits their use. By stopping cooking for him, I might have solved my immediate frustration, but it's causing problems for him. This could lead to tension in our relationship and make living together more difficult. In conclusion, while I think I did what I felt was necessary to protect my feelings, it might be considered AITA because I didn't fully consider the impact of my decision on my roommate. It might have been better to find a compromise or continue the conversation to find a solution that works for both of us.
